audience: beginner to intermediate developers, students, English + some Russian speakers, UTC+5 evenings most active
cta_patterns: Telegram native Poll right after post (quiz: $ ANSWER_REQUIRED: / > OUTPUT_REQUIRED: with 4 options; community: > FUEL_REQUIRED: / $ SELECT_TIME:)
inline directives: Vote below. / Think before running it. 👀 / Run it. Then tell us: / Join the workshop...
workshop flow: announcement -> $ SELECT_TIME: poll -> $ DECISION: -> countdown posts -> WE_ARE_STARTING
difficulty_rules: quizzes are medium: one tricky concept (references, associativity, mutation during iteration, copy vs reference). Never trivial, never leetcode-hard.
emoji_usage: moderate, 2-6 per post. Signature set: 🐍 👾 ⚡ 🔥 🧠 👀 🤯 🏆 📍 💻 🍿 🍪. Reactions to aim for: 🔥 ⚡ 👾 🤯 💯. Never random emoji spam.
format_rules: > HEADER lines are UPPERCASE with > prefix: > QUIZ_02, > QUIZ_02.SOLUTION, > SYSTEM_UPDATE, > WORKSHOP_01, > DEV_CONFESSION_01, > WHY?, > WHAT_IS_THE_OUTPUT?
$ VARIABLE lines are lowercase snake_case with $ prefix, often trailing underscore: $ EXECUTE_THE_CODE:, $ CORRECT_OUTPUT:, $ KEY_IDEA:, $ think_before_you_run_, $ status:, $ schedule:, $ ACCESS:
separator style: LANGUAGE: { python } / DIFFICULTY: { medium } on separate lines for newer quizzes
code is plain monospace block, 3-8 lines, no syntax highlighting markup — Telegram renders it raw
explanations use short lines with hard breaks, ASCII diagrams allowed (x ──┐ / ▼ / [1,2])
no hashtags, no markdown links except bare platform URL or t.me link
post + poll are TWO messages: content post first, poll second
language: English primary. Short punchy sentences. Code-switch to Russian only for jokes (YOPTASCRIPT) or bilingual workshop notes (English / Russian).
post_length: short: 40-130 words + code. Solutions slightly longer (100-180 words) due to WHY? + KEY_IDEA diagram.
quiz_structure: header (> QUIZ_NN) → > LANGUAGE: X → $ execute_the_code: → code → > WHAT_IS_THE_OUTPUT? → CTA (Think before running it. 👀). Poll follows: $ ANSWER_REQUIRED: with 4 options. Solution next day: > QUIZ_NN.SOLUTION → $ CORRECT_OUTPUT: → > [answer] → stats (NN% got it right. 👀/📈) → > WHY? → step-by-step → $ KEY_IDEA: → > one-line rule → > THINK_BEFORE_YOU_RUN. 🧠
solution_structure: answer → % correct stats → WHY? step trace → $ KEY_IDEA: one rule → CTA think_before_you_run_
tone: friendly, nerdy, concise, playful-direct. Speaks like a terminal that likes you: STATUS updates, INPUT_REQUIRED prompts, teasing but encouraging. Never corporate, never generic-AI.
visual_style: dark terminal / lime accent. Attached media: 1280x720 dark code-card for quizzes, ASCII/terminal screenshots for IT facts, memes as video/animation + poll.
workshop_structure: > WORKSHOP_NN → hook (We've been throwing quizzes...) → $ first_online_workshop: → [ 📍 ] discord / [ 💻 ] pc required / [ 🌐 ] English / Russian → > we'll: → arrow list → $ schedule: → > WAITING_FOR_INPUT_ → poll $ SELECT_TIME: (19:00/20:00/21:00) → $ DECISION: → → 21:00 ✅ → countdown ($ STARTING_IN: 10 MINUTES) → WE_ARE_STARTING!!! → next-day ATTENDANCE_LOG + PLATFORM update
